Integrate the differential equation dP/dr = ρ·r·ω² to obtain the radial pressure distribution in a rotating fluid.
The angular velocity is ω = 2π × 10000 / 60 rad/s, which equals approximately 1047.2 rad/s.
The density ρ is a symbolic parameter; no specific fluid or numerical density value is assigned.
The integrated result is P(r) = ½ρ·ω²·r² + C, where C is an undetermined integration constant.
Express the final result as a pressure difference relative to the axis: P(r) − P(0) = ½ρ·ω²·r².
Do not assign a numerical value to C or impose a specific boundary pressure at any radius.
The deliverable is the closed-form expression demonstrating that pressure varies quadratically with radial distance from the rotation axis.
No specific outer radius, chamber geometry, or numerical pressure value is required in the output.
